before.zh: [一]閉諸陽，衣皁，興土龍，[二]立土人舞僮二佾，七日一變如故事。
before.en: First, seal every yang portal, dress in black, and raise earthen dragons; second, station clay effigies and two ranks of boy dancers, altering the setup every seven days as statute prescribes.
before.literal: [One] Close off all yang [omens]; wear black clothing; erect clay dragons; [two] set up clay figures and boy dancers in two rows (yi); once every seven days change [the arrangement] according to precedent.

after.zh: [一]閉諸陽，衣皁，興土龍，[二]立土人舞僮二佾，七日一變如故事。
after.en: Seal every yang portal, dress in black, and raise earthen dragons; station clay effigies and two ranks of boy dancers, altering the setup every seven days as statute prescribes.
after.literal: [One] Close off all yang [omens]; wear black clothing; erect clay dragons; [two] set up clay figures and boy dancers in two rows (yi); once every seven days change [the arrangement] according to precedent.

before.zh: [三]反拘朱索*[縈]*社，伐朱鼓。
before.en: Third, reverse the bindings, loop red cords around the soil altar, and beat the crimson drum.
before.literal: [Three] Invert [the cord], bind red cords [coiling] around the she altar, and strike the red drum.

after.zh: [三]反拘朱索*[縈]*社，伐朱鼓。
after.en: Reverse the bindings, loop red cords around the soil altar, and beat the crimson drum.
after.literal: [Three] Invert [the cord], bind red cords [coiling] around the she altar, and strike the red drum.

before.zh: [四]禱賽以少牢如禮。
before.en: Fourth, offer prayer and votive thanks with a pig-and-goat set, following canonical form.
before.literal: [Four] Pray and give thanks with a lesser sacrifice (shao lao) according to the rites.

before.zh: 暴巫聚蛇八日。
before.en: For eight days shamans sun themselves in the open while snakes are assembled—per Dong Zhongshu's liturgy.
before.literal: Expose the witches and gather snakes for eight days.

after.zh: 暴巫聚蛇八日。
after.en: For eight days shamans sun themselves in the open while snakes are assembled.
after.literal: Expose the witches and gather snakes for eight days.

before.zh: 譚問：『求雨所以為土龍，何也？』
before.en: Huan Tan asks why clay dragons are fashioned when praying for rain.
before.literal: Tan asked: 'For seeking rain, the reason one makes clay dragons—what is it?'

after.zh: 譚問：『求雨所以為土龍，何也？』
after.en: I, Tan, asked: 'Why are clay dragons made when seeking rain?'
after.literal: Tan asked: 'For seeking rain, the reason one makes clay dragons—what is it?'

before.zh: 注[二]丁孚漢儀有夏勤策文，曰：「維元初六年三月甲子，制詔以大鴻臚勤為司徒。
before.en: Comment 2 preserves Xia Qin's patent: "Yuanchu 6, third month, jiazi—the Grand Herald becomes Minister of Education.
before.literal: Comment [two]: Ding Fu's Han Observances contains Xia Qin's edict text, saying: "On the jiazi day of the third month, sixth year of Yuanchu, the sealed edict appoints the Grand Herald Qin as Minister of Education.

before.zh: 故有莘興殷，姜任母周，二代之隆，蓋有內德。
before.en: Youxin's bride founded Yin; Jiang Yuan mothered Zhou—both golden ages rested on inner virtue.
before.literal: Therefore Youxin raised Yin; Jiang Ren mothered Zhou; the glory of the two ages surely had inner virtue.

after.zh: 故有莘興殷，姜任母周，二代之隆，蓋有內德。
after.en: The woman of Youxin made Yin flourish; Tai Jiang and Tai Ren mothered Zhou—both golden ages rested on inner virtue.
after.literal: Therefore Youxin raised Yin; Jiang Ren mothered Zhou; the glory of the two ages surely had inner virtue.

before.zh: 今使太尉襲使持節奉璽綬，宗正祖為副，立貴人為皇后。
before.en: The Grand Commandant, credential in hand, presents the regalia with the Director of the Imperial Clan as deputy, raising the Honored Lady to empress.
before.literal: Now dispatch the Grand Commandant Xi as bearer of the staff of authority to present the seal-ribbons; the Director of the Imperial Clan Zu serves as deputy; establish the Honored Lady as empress.

after.zh: 今使太尉襲使持節奉璽綬，宗正祖為副，立貴人為皇后。
after.en: Grand Commandant Xi, credential in hand, presents the regalia with the Director of the Imperial Clan Zu as deputy, raising the Honored Lady to empress.

before.zh: **[秋]*太僕高鄉侯覽長跪受璽綬，奏於殿前，女史授婕妤，婕妤長跪受，以授昭儀，昭儀受，長跪以帶皇后。
before.en: The Coachman Lan receives the case before the throne; female attendants pass it from Handmaid to Bright Companion to belt the empress.
before.literal: [Qiu] Grand Coachman Marquis of Gaoxiang Lan kneels long receiving the seal-ribbons, presents them before the hall; the female scribe hands them to the Lady of Handsome Fairness; the Lady of Handsome Fairness kneels long receiving, and hands them to the Lady of Bright Deportment; the Lady of Bright Deportment receives, kneels long, and belts the empress.

after.zh: **[秋]*太僕高鄉侯覽長跪受璽綬，奏於殿前，女史授婕妤，婕妤長跪受，以授昭儀，昭儀受，長跪以帶皇后。
after.en: The Palace Regular Attendant and Coachman of the Changle Palace, Lan, Marquis of Gaoxiang, kneels to receive the case before the throne; female attendants pass it from Handmaid to Bright Companion to belt the empress.
after.literal: [Qiu] Grand Coachman Marquis of Gaoxiang Lan kneels long receiving the seal-ribbons, presents them before the hall; the female scribe hands them to the Lady of Handsome Fairness; the Lady of Handsome Fairness kneels long receiving, and hands them to the Lady of Bright Deportment; the Lady of Bright Deportment receives, kneels long, and belts the empress.

before.zh: 至立秋，迎氣於黃郊，樂奏黃鐘之宮，歌帝臨，冕而執干戚，舞雲翹、育命，所以養時訓也。
before.en: At autumn's advent they greet yellow qi in the southern suburb with Yellow Bell music, the hymn "Imperial Presence," shield dances, and the Cloud and Nurture dances to tune the season.
before.literal: By Beginning of Autumn, they welcome qi at the yellow suburb; music plays the Yellow Bell palace mode; they sing "The Emperor Approaches"; wearing crown they hold shield and axe; they dance Cloud Rising and Nurturing the Mandate—by this they nurture seasonal instruction.

after.zh: 至立秋，迎氣於黃郊，樂奏黃鐘之宮，歌帝臨，冕而執干戚，舞雲翹、育命，所以養時訓也。
after.en: At autumn's advent they greet yellow qi at the yellow suburb with Yellow Bell music, the hymn "Imperial Presence," shield dances, and the Cloud and Nurture dances to tune the season.
after.literal: By Beginning of Autumn, they welcome qi at the yellow suburb; music plays the Yellow Bell palace mode; they sing "The Emperor Approaches"; wearing crown they hold shield and axe; they dance Cloud Rising and Nurturing the Mandate—by this they nurture seasonal instruction.

before.zh: 乘輿御戎路，白馬朱鬣，躬執弩射牲。
before.en: The emperor rides the martial avenue on a white horse with crimson mane and personally bolts the quarry with a crossbow.
before.literal: The imperial carriage mounts the war chariot road [route]; white horse, vermilion mane; personally handles crossbow and shoots the victim.

after.zh: 乘輿御戎路，白馬朱鬣，躬執弩射牲。

before.zh: 兵、官皆肄孫、吳兵法六十四陣，名曰乘之。
before.en: Commanders and men drill the sixty-four Sun Wu formations known as the maneuver.
before.literal: Soldiers and officers both drill Sun and Wu's Art of War sixty-four formations—called 'riding it.'

after.zh: 兵、官皆肄孫、吳兵法六十四陣，名曰乘之。
after.en: Commanders and men drill the sixty-four formations of the Sun (Sunzi) and Wu (Wu Qi) arts of war known as the maneuver.
after.literal: Soldiers and officers both drill Sun and Wu's Art of War sixty-four formations—called 'riding it.'

before.zh: [四]貙劉之禮：祠先虞，執事告先虞已，烹鮮時，有司*[告]*，乃逡巡射牲。
before.en: The Chu Liu opens with Forester Yu; once officers announce readiness they rotate inward and loose at the beast.
before.literal: [Four] Chu Liu ritual: sacrifice to Forester Yu; when attendants report Forester Yu complete, at cooking-the-fresh time, the officers [report], then deferentially circle and shoot the victim.

after.zh: [四]貙劉之禮：祠先虞，執事告先虞已，烹鮮時，有司*[告]*，乃逡巡射牲。
after.en: The Chu Liu opens with a sacrifice to the First Forester (Xian Yu); once officers announce readiness they rotate inward and loose at the beast.
after.literal: [Four] Chu Liu ritual: sacrifice to Forester Yu; when attendants report Forester Yu complete, at cooking-the-fresh time, the officers [report], then deferentially circle and shoot the victim.

before.zh: 漢承秦制，三時不講，唯十月車駕幸長安水南門，會五營士，為八陣進退，名曰乘之。
before.en: Han followed Qin by drilling chiefly in the tenth month at Chang'an's south gate with the five camps wheeling through eight arrays.
before.literal: Han inherited Qin institutions; three seasons did not drill; only in the tenth month the carriage visits Chang'an Water South Gate, convenes five-camp soldiers, performs eight formations advance and retreat—called 'riding it.'

after.zh: 漢承秦制，三時不講，唯十月車駕幸長安水南門，會五營士，為八陣進退，名曰乘之。
after.en: Han followed Qin: no drills in three seasons, only in the tenth month the emperor went to the south gate of Chang'an by the river, assembled the troops of the five camps and ran the eight formations, called 'chengzhi'.
after.literal: Han inherited Qin institutions; three seasons did not drill; only in the tenth month the carriage visits Chang'an Water South Gate, convenes five-camp soldiers, performs eight formations advance and retreat—called 'riding it.'

before.zh: 又校補引柳從辰說，謂成帝建始四年罷中書官，以中書為中謁者令，見漢舊儀，作「甲」非。
before.en: Liu’s point is that “first” is impossible once the Secretariat had become the Central Herald office; the graph should not read jia.
before.literal: The collators also cite Liu Congchen: in Chengdi’s fourth year of Jianshi the Secretariat office was abolished and its director was made Director of the Central Herald—see the Han Old Ceremonies—so writing jia is incorrect.

after.zh: 又校補引柳從辰說，謂成帝建始四年罷中書官，以中書為中謁者令，見漢舊儀，作「甲」非。
after.en: The Collation Supplement cites Liu Congchen: in Jianshi 4 Emperor Cheng abolished the Secretariat (eunuch) office, making the Secretariat the Palace Herald Director (per the Han Old Observances), so the reading jia is wrong.
after.literal: The collators also cite Liu Congchen: in Chengdi’s fourth year of Jianshi the Secretariat office was abolished and its director was made Director of the Central Herald—see the Han Old Ceremonies—so writing jia is incorrect.

before.en: Page 3121, line 6: "in the sixth year of Yuanchu, in the third month." Note: Lu Yun observes that according to Emperor An's Annals, in the third year of Yongchu, in the fourth month, on bingyin, Xia Qin, Chamberlain for Dependencies, became Minister over the Masses.
before.literal: Folio 3121, line 6: “In the third month of the sixth year of Yuanchu”—Comment: Lu checks the Annals of Emperor An: in the fourth month, bingyin day, of Yongchu 3, the Grand Herald Xia Qin became Minister of Education.

after.literal: Folio 3121, line 6: “In the third month of the sixth year of Yuanchu”—Comment: Lu checks the Annals of Emperor An: in the fourth month, bingyin day, of Yongchu 3, the Grand Herald Xia Qin became Minister of Education.

after.en: If it were the Yuanchu era, Liu Kai had already replaced Xia Qin.
after.literal: If the text truly meant the Yuanchu period, then Liu Kai would be the one who succeeded Qin.

before.zh: 三一二一頁一四行維建寧四年七月乙未集解引錢大昕說，謂靈帝紀作「七月癸丑」。
before.en: Qian notes that the Annals of Emperor Ling read "seventh month, guichou day" for the same ceremony.
before.literal: Folio 3121, line 14: “On the yiwei day of the seventh month in the fourth year of Jianning”—Collected glosses cite Qian Daxin: the Annals of Emperor Ling read “seventh month, guichou day.”

after.zh: 三一二一頁一四行維建寧四年七月乙未集解引錢大昕說，謂靈帝紀作「七月癸丑」。
after.en: The Jijie cites Qian Daxin, who notes that the Annals of Emperor Ling read "seventh month, guichou day" for the same ceremony.
after.literal: Folio 3121, line 14: “On the yiwei day of the seventh month in the fourth year of Jianning”—Collected glosses cite Qian Daxin: the Annals of Emperor Ling read “seventh month, guichou day.”

before.zh: 三一二二頁一行今使太尉襲持節奉璽綬按：集解引錢大昕說，謂案靈帝紀，太尉聞人襲以三月免官，此立後乃在七月，或紀所書月日誤。
before.en: Qian flags a mismatch between the marriage edict and Wenren Xi’s tenure.
before.literal: Folio 3122, line 1: “We now send Grand Commandant Xi, baton in hand, to present the seal and ribbon”—Comment: Collected glosses cite Qian Daxin: the Annals of Emperor Ling show Grand Commandant Wenren Xi dismissed in the third month, whereas this investiture falls in the seventh—perhaps the annals’ month is wrong.

after.zh: 三一二二頁一行今使太尉襲持節奉璽綬按：集解引錢大昕說，謂案靈帝紀，太尉聞人襲以三月免官，此立後乃在七月，或紀所書月日誤。
after.en: Qian Daxin notes that per the Annals of Emperor Ling, Grand Commandant Wenren Xi was dismissed in the third month, whereas the empress was invested in the seventh; perhaps the Annals' month is wrong.
after.literal: Folio 3122, line 1: “We now send Grand Commandant Xi, baton in hand, to present the seal and ribbon”—Comment: Collected glosses cite Qian Daxin: the Annals of Emperor Ling show Grand Commandant Wenren Xi dismissed in the third month, whereas this investiture falls in the seventh—perhaps the annals’ month is wrong.

before.zh: 三一二八頁四行司馬闕門門外按：集解引黃山說，謂秦蕙田據舊本，「門外」作「之外」。
before.en: Witnesses disagree on whether the clause repeats ‘gate’ or uses ‘beyond.’
before.literal: Folio 3128, line 4: ‘The marshal leaves the gate outside the gate’—Comment: Collected glosses cite Huang Shan: Qin Huitian’s old edition reads ‘beyond’ for ‘outside.’

after.zh: 三一二八頁四行司馬闕門門外按：集解引黃山說，謂秦蕙田據舊本，「門外」作「之外」。
after.en: The Jijie cites Huang Shan: Qin Huitian, following an old edition, reads wai zhi (outside) for men wai (outside the gate).
after.literal: Folio 3128, line 4: ‘The marshal leaves the gate outside the gate’—Comment: Collected glosses cite Huang Shan: Qin Huitian’s old edition reads ‘beyond’ for ‘outside.’

before.zh: 按：此劉昭引韋昭注國語文，「臣」當作「韋」。
before.en: The surname was miscopied as chen ‘minister.’
before.literal: Comment: here Liu Zhao cites Wei Zhao’s Guoyu commentary; chen should be Wei.

after.zh: 按：此劉昭引韋昭注國語文，「臣」當作「韋」。
after.en: Here Liu Zhao quotes Wei Zhao's commentary on the Guoyu; the character chen ('minister') should read Wei (for Wei Zhao).
after.literal: Comment: here Liu Zhao cites Wei Zhao’s Guoyu commentary; chen should be Wei.

before.zh: 三一二九頁一行一名沐□按：汲本、殿本「□」作「□」，盧文弨依國語韋注改為「腫」。
before.en: Folio 3129, line 1: ‘First name Mu[lacuna]’—Comment: Ji and Palace editions show a lacuna for another lacuna; Lu Wencha follows the Guoyu Wei commentary in reading zhong ‘swelling demon.’
